authoring.question: q-339239
authoring.value: The population $P(t)$ of fish in a pond after $t$ weeks can be modeled by the differential equation ${P}^{′}(t)=0.09P(t).$ If the fish population was $8\,000$ after $18$ weeks, calculate the fish population after $23$ weeks. Round the final population to the nearest whole fish. Do not round intermediate values.
authoring.rationale: The source lesson rounds the initial constant to three decimal places, then rounds the resulting later population to 12,547. That is its documented approximation method, confirmed by the revealed source solution. The study prompt now explicitly requires final-only nearest-whole rounding, whose mathematically correct value is 12,546. Preserve original source content and its 12,547 key in historical question content and immutable old answer fields; create new study field and answer identities with matching prompt, solution, choice and key.

decisions.reason: Retain the verified mathematical correction instead of reimporting the source error

authoring.value:
The solution of $P'(t)=0.09P(t)$ satisfies

$$P(t)=P(18)e^{0.09(t-18)}=8\,000e^{0.09(t-18)}.$$

Therefore,

$$P(23)=8\,000e^{0.45}\approx12\,546.49748392135.$$

Rounding only this final value to the nearest whole number gives approximately $12\,546$ fish.
